cur:monumental-sma-christ-enthroned-fath.summary: Along the left aisle, a long row of standing saints and Fathers of the Western and Eastern Churches converges on the enthroned Christ at the centre, while scenes from the Old Testament stories of Noah and Joseph run in a frieze above. The great wall gathers the whole Church, Latin and Greek, around Christ.
facts: Santa Maria Antiqua in the Roman Forum preserves wall paintings from the 6th to the late 8th century; buried after an earthquake in 847, it was rediscovered only in 1900.
Inscriptions in the church shift from Greek (under Martin I) to Greek and Latin (under John VII) and finally Latin alone (under Paul I), reflecting Rome's changing ties to Byzantium.
